units.zh: 楊行密，廬州人。
units.en: Yang Xingmi was a native of Luzhou.
units.literal: Yang Xingmi was a man of Luzhou.

units.zh: 少孤貧，有膂力，日行三百里。
units.en: He lost his parents early and grew up poor, but he was powerfully built and could cover three hundred li on foot in a single day.
units.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he had great physical strength and could travel three hundred li in a day on foot.

units.zh: 唐中和之亂，天子幸蜀，郡將遣行密徒步奏事，如期而復。
units.en: During the Tang Zhonghe disorders, when the emperor fled to Shu, the local commander sent Xingmi on foot to deliver reports to the court, and he returned exactly on time.
units.literal: During the Zhonghe turmoil of the Tang, when the Son of Heaven took refuge in Shu, the prefectural commander sent Xingmi on foot to report to the court; he returned on schedule.

units.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》：鄭綮嘗典楊行密為本州步奏官。）〉
units.en: (The 《Beimeng Suoyan》 records that Zheng Qi and Yang Xingmi had once both served as foot couriers for their prefecture.)
units.literal: (The 《Beimeng Suoyan》 says: Zheng Qi once served together with Yang Xingmi as a foot-messenger officer for the prefecture.)

units.zh: 光啟初，秦宗權擾淮右，頻寇廬、壽，郡將募能致戰擒賊者，計級賞之，行密以膽力應募，往必有獲，得補為隊長。
units.en: Early in Guangqi, Qin Zongquan ravaged the Huai region and repeatedly struck Luzhou and Shouzhou. The prefect recruited men who could fight and bring back prisoners, paying by the head. Xingmi enlisted on the strength of his nerve and brawn; every sortie brought captures, and he was made a squad leader.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Guangqi reign, Qin Zongquan harassed the right bank of the Huai, frequently raiding Luzhou and Shouzhou; the prefectural commander recruited men who could bring battle and capture bandits, rewarding them by the head count. Xingmi volunteered for his courage and strength, and whenever he went out he was sure to take captives, and was appointed a squad leader.

units.zh: 行密乃自募百餘人，皆璟勇無行者，殺都將，自權州兵，郡將即以符印付之而去，朝廷因正授行密廬州刺史。
units.en: Xingmi then raised over a hundred men of his own, every one a ferocious fighter who would not keep ranks. They killed the garrison commander and took command of the prefectural army. The prefect surrendered his seal and left, and the court formally appointed Xingmi prefect of Luzhou.
units.literal: Xingmi then recruited more than a hundred men on his own, all fiercely bold but undisciplined in marching; they killed the commander-in-chief, seized control of the prefectural troops, and the prefectural commander thereupon handed over the seal and credentials and departed. The court thereupon formally appointed Xingmi prefect of Luzhou.

units.zh: 光啟三年，揚州節度使高駢失政，委任妖人呂用之輩。
units.en: In the third year of Guangqi, Gao Pian, military governor of Yangzhou, misgoverned and put his trust in charlatans like Lü Yongzhi.
units.literal: In the third year of Guangqi, Yangzhou military governor Gao Pian lost control of government and entrusted affairs to sorcerers such as Lü Yongzhi and his ilk.

units.zh: 牙將畢師鐸懼為用之所譖，自高郵起兵以襲廣陵，為用之所卻，乃乞師於宣州秦彥，且言事克之日，願以揚州帥之。
units.en: Guards general Bi Shiduo, fearing Lü Yongzhi would frame him, marched from Gaoyou against Guangling but was driven back. He then asked Qin Yan of Xuanzhou for reinforcements, promising that if they won, Yan could have the Yangzhou command.
units.literal: The guards general Bi Shiduo, fearing slander by Yongzhi, raised troops from Gaoyou to attack Guangling, but was repelled by Yongzhi; he then begged troops from Qin Yan of Xuanzhou, and moreover said that when the affair was accomplished he wished to make Yan commander of Yangzhou.

units.zh: 彥先遣將秦稠以兵三千人助師鐸攻陷廣陵，高駢署師鐸為行軍司馬。
units.en: Yan first sent Qin Chou with three thousand men to help Shiduo take Guangling. Gao Pian named Shiduo acting army marshal.
units.literal: Yan first sent the general Qin Chou with three thousand troops to help Shiduo capture Guangling; Gao Pian appointed Shiduo acting army marshal.

units.zh: 未幾，秦彥率大眾並家屬渡江，入揚州軍府，自稱節度使。
units.en: Soon afterward Qin Yan crossed the Yangzi at the head of a large force, families in tow, seized the Yangzhou headquarters, and declared himself military governor.
units.literal: Before long, Qin Yan led a great host together with his household across the river, entered the Yangzhou military headquarters, and styled himself military governor.

units.zh: 初，揚州未陷，呂用之詐為高駢檄，征兵於廬州，及城陷，行密以萬人奄至。
units.en: Before Yangzhou fell, Lü Yongzhi had forged an order in Gao Pian's name to raise troops in Luzhou. When the city collapsed, Xingmi swept in with ten thousand men.
units.literal: Earlier, before Yangzhou had fallen, Lü Yongzhi forged a dispatch in Gao Pian's name to levy troops at Luzhou; when the city fell, Xingmi arrived suddenly with ten thousand men.

units.zh: 畢師鐸之入廣陵也，呂用之出奔於外，至是委質於行密。
units.en: When Bi Shiduo took Guangling, Lü Yongzhi had fled into the countryside; now he surrendered to Xingmi.
units.literal: When Bi Shiduo entered Guangling, Lü Yongzhi had fled abroad; at this time he submitted to Xingmi.

units.zh: 行密攻廣陵，營於大明寺，秦、畢出兵以攻行密之營，短兵才接，行密偽遁，秦、畢之兵爭入其柵，以取金帛，行密發伏兵以擊之，秦、畢大敗，退走其壁，自是不復出戰。
units.en: Xingmi besieged Guangling and pitched camp at Daming Temple. Qin and Bi attacked his lines; at the first clash Xingmi pretended to flee. Their men stormed his camp for loot, and his ambushers cut them down. Qin and Bi were routed back to their walls and never offered battle again.
units.literal: Xingmi attacked Guangling and encamped at Daming Temple. Qin and Bi led troops to assault Xingmi's camp; as soon as the melee joined, Xingmi feigned retreat. The troops of Qin and Bi rushed into his palisade to seize gold and silks; Xingmi unleashed ambush troops to strike them, and Qin and Bi were utterly defeated, fleeing back to their ramparts, and from then on did not come out to fight again.

units.zh: 其年九月，秦、畢害高駢於幽所，少長皆死，同坎痤於道院北垣下。
units.en: That September, Qin and Bi murdered Gao Pian in confinement, killing his household to the last, and buried them together in a single pit below the north wall of the abbey.
units.literal: In the ninth month of that year, Qin and Bi killed Gao Pian in his place of confinement; young and old alike perished, and were buried together in one pit beneath the north wall of the Daoist abbey.

units.zh: 行密攻圍彌急，城中食盡，米斗四十千，居人相啖略盡。
units.en: Xingmi tightened the siege until the city was starving; rice sold for forty thousand cash a dou, and the people had nearly eaten one another.
units.literal: Xingmi pressed the siege ever tighter; food in the city was exhausted, and rice reached forty thousand cash per dou; the inhabitants had nearly devoured one another.

units.zh: 十月，城陷，秦、畢走東塘，行密入廣陵，輦外寨之粟以食饑民，即日米價減至三千。
units.en: In the tenth month the city fell. Qin and Bi fled to Dongtang while Xingmi entered Guangling, hauled grain from the outer camps to feed the hungry, and the same day rice fell to three thousand cash a dou.
units.literal: In the tenth month the city fell; Qin and Bi fled to Dongtang. Xingmi entered Guangling, carted grain from the outer camps to feed the starving people, and that same day the price of rice fell to three thousand.

units.zh: 十一月，蔡賊孫儒以眾萬人自淮西奄至，還據外寨，行密輜重牛羊軍食未入城者，皆為儒所有。
units.en: In the eleventh month the Cai bandit Sun Ru swept in from west of the Huai with ten thousand men, seized the outer camps again, and took everything Xingmi had left outside the walls—baggage, livestock, and army stores.
units.literal: In the eleventh month, the Cai rebel Sun Ru arrived suddenly from west of the Huai with a host of ten thousand, reoccupied the outer camps, and all of Xingmi's baggage, cattle, sheep, and army provisions that had not yet entered the city fell into Ru's possession.

units.zh: 時秦、畢來自東塘，與儒軍合，自是西門之外，復為敵境矣。
units.en: Qin and Bi now came up from Dongtang and joined Sun Ru, so everything beyond the west gate was enemy country once more.
units.literal: At that time Qin and Bi came from Dongtang and joined Ru's army; from then on, beyond the west gate it again became enemy territory.

units.zh: 初，呂用之遇行密於天長，紿行密曰：「用之有白金五千鋌，瘞於所居之廡下，寇平之日，願備將士倡樓一醉之資。」
units.en: Earlier, at Tianchang, Lü Yongzhi had told Xingmi a lie: he claimed five thousand ingots of silver were buried under his quarters and promised that once the rebels were crushed he would pay for a feast for the whole army."
units.literal: Earlier, when Lü Yongzhi met Xingmi at Tianchang, he deceived Xingmi, saying, "Yongzhi has five thousand ingots of white metal buried beneath the eaves of my dwelling; when the bandits are pacified, I wish to provide funds for the officers and soldiers to carouse once in the tower."

units.zh: 至是，行密閱兵，用之在側，謂用之曰：「僕射許此輩銀，何負心也！」
units.en: Now, as Xingmi reviewed the troops with Yongzhi beside him, he said, "You promised these men silver, Vice Director—where is your word?"
units.literal: At this time Xingmi reviewed the troops with Yongzhi at his side and said to Yongzhi, "Vice Director, you promised silver to these men—how faithless!"

units.zh: 遽命斬於三橋之下，夷其族。
units.en: He had him beheaded at once below the Three Bridges and wiped out his family.
units.literal: He immediately ordered him beheaded beneath the Three Bridges and exterminated his clan.

units.zh: 行密既有廣陵，遣使至大梁，陳歸附之意。
units.en: After Xingmi secured Guangling, he sent envoys to Daliang to declare his submission.
units.literal: Once Xingmi held Guangling, he sent envoys to Daliang to declare his intent to submit.

units.zh: 是時，梁祖兼領淮南，乃遣牙將張廷範使於淮南，與行密結盟，尋遣行軍司馬李璠權知淮南留後，令都將郭言以兵援送。
units.en: The Liang Founder then held Huainan as well. He sent guards officer Zhang Tingfan to ally with Xingmi, then dispatched acting army marshal Li Fan as provisional regent of Huainan, with commander Guo Yan escorting him at the head of an army.
units.literal: At that time the Liang Founder also held Huainan concurrently; he therefore sent the guards general Zhang Tingfan as envoy to Huainan to ally with Xingmi, and soon afterward sent the acting army marshal Li Fan as provisional Huainan regent, ordering the commander-in-chief Guo Yan to escort him with troops.

units.zh: 行密初則厚禮廷範，及聞李璠之行，勃然有拒命之意。
units.en: Xingmi first received Tingfan with full honors, but when he learned Li Fan was coming he flared up and made clear he would not obey.
units.literal: Xingmi at first treated Tingfan with great courtesy, but when he heard of Li Fan's mission he suddenly showed intent to defy orders.

units.zh: 廷範懼，易衣夜遁，遇梁祖於宋州，備言行密不軌之心，酌其兵勢未可圖也，乃追李璠等還，即表行密為淮南留後。
units.en: Tingfan, terrified, changed clothes and fled by night. He met the Liang Founder at Songzhou and reported Xingmi's rebellious mood. Judging that Xingmi's forces could not yet be crushed, the Founder recalled Li Fan and memorialized to make Xingmi Huainan regent.
units.literal: Tingfan was afraid, changed clothes and fled by night, met the Liang Founder at Songzhou, and reported fully Xingmi's disloyal intent; weighing that his military strength could not yet be overcome, the Founder then recalled Li Fan and the others, and immediately memorialized to appoint Xingmi Huainan regent.

units.zh: 文德元年正月，孫儒殺秦彥、畢師鐸於高郵，引軍襲廣陵，下之，儒自稱節度使，行密收其眾歸於廬江。
units.en: In the first month of Wende 1, Sun Ru killed Qin Yan and Bi Shiduo at Gaoyou, stormed and took Guangling, and declared himself military governor. Xingmi gathered what forces he could and fell back to Lujiang.
units.literal: In the first month of the first year of Wende, Sun Ru killed Qin Yan and Bi Shiduo at Gaoyou, led his army to strike Guangling, captured it, and Ru styled himself military governor; Xingmi gathered his troops and withdrew to Lujiang.

units.zh: 十一月，梁祖遣大將龐師古自潁上渡淮，討孫儒之亂，師古引兵深入淮甸，不利，還。
units.en: In the eleventh month the Liang Founder sent Pang Shigu from Yingshang across the Huai against Sun Ru. Shigu pushed deep into the Huai country, met reverses, and withdrew.
units.literal: In the eleventh month the Liang Founder sent the great general Pang Shigu from Yingshang across the Huai to suppress Sun Ru's rebellion; Shigu led his troops deep into the Huai region, met with ill fortune, and returned.

units.zh: 龍紀元年，孫儒出攻宣州，行密乘虛襲據揚州，北通時溥，孫儒引兵復攻行密。
units.en: In Longji 1, Sun Ru marched on Xuanzhou. Xingmi seized the opening, stormed Yangzhou, and allied northward with Shi Pu. Sun Ru turned back to attack him.
units.literal: In the first year of Longji, Sun Ru marched out to attack Xuanzhou; Xingmi seized the opportunity to strike and occupy Yangzhou, opened relations northward with Shi Pu, and Sun Ru led his army back to attack Xingmi.

units.zh: 大順元年，行密危蹙，率眾夜遁，出據宣州，儒復入揚州。
units.en: In Dashun 1, Xingmi was hard pressed, broke out by night, and held Xuanzhou while Ru reoccupied Yangzhou.
units.literal: In the first year of Dashun, Xingmi was in dire straits, led his host in flight by night, went out and seized Xuanzhou, and Ru re-entered Yangzhou.

units.zh: 二年，乃蒐練兵甲以攻行密，屬江、淮疾疫，師人多死，儒亦臥病，為部下所執，送於行密，殺之。
units.en: The next year he mustered arms to strike Xingmi again, but plague swept the Jiang-Huai country and decimated his army. Ru himself fell ill, was seized by his own men, handed to Xingmi, and executed.
units.literal: In the second year he then gathered and drilled armor and weapons to attack Xingmi; just then plague struck the Jiang and Huai regions, and many soldiers died. Ru also took to his bed with illness, was seized by his subordinates, sent to Xingmi, and killed.

units.zh: 行密自宣城長驅入於廣陵，盡得孫儒之眾。
units.en: Xingmi swept from Xuancheng into Guangling and absorbed Sun Ru's entire army.
units.literal: Xingmi drove at full speed from Xuancheng into Guangling and wholly took over Sun Ru's forces.

units.zh: 自光啟末，高駢失守之後，行密與畢師鐸、秦彥、孫儒遞相窺圖，六七年中，兵革競起，八州之內，鞠為荒榛，圜幅數百里，人煙斷絕。
units.en: From late Guangqi, after Gao Pian's fall, Xingmi, Bi Shiduo, Qin Yan, and Sun Ru had eyed one another's territories in turn. For six or seven years war never stopped; across eight prefectures the land turned to wilderness, and for hundreds of li in every direction no smoke rose from any hearth.
units.literal: From late Guangqi, after Gao Pian lost his hold, Xingmi with Bi Shiduo, Qin Yan, and Sun Ru watched and plotted against one another in turn; for six or seven years arms clashed everywhere, and within the eight prefectures all became wasteland thicket; for several hundred li in every direction human habitation ceased.

units.zh: 行密既並孫儒，乃招合遺散，與民休息，政事寬簡，百姓便之，蒐兵練將，以圖霸道。
units.en: After defeating Sun Ru, Xingmi gathered the displaced, gave the people respite, and ruled with a light hand that the common folk welcomed. He rebuilt his armies and trained his commanders, aiming at supremacy.
units.literal: Once Xingmi had absorbed Sun Ru, he then gathered the scattered remnant, let the people rest, made government lenient and simple so the common people found it convenient, and collected troops and trained generals to scheme for hegemony.

units.zh: 所得孫儒之眾，皆淮南之驍果也，選五千人豢養於府第，厚其衣食，驅之既戰，靡不爭先。
units.en: Sun Ru's soldiers were the hardiest fighters in Huainan. Xingmi picked five thousand, housed them in his mansion, fed and clothed them lavishly, and whenever he sent them into battle they fought to be first.
units.literal: The troops taken from Sun Ru were all the fiercest fighters of Huainan; he chose five thousand men to rear within his headquarters residence, lavished food and clothing on them, and whenever he drove them into battle none failed to vie for the front.

units.zh: 甲胄皆以黑繒飾之，命曰「黑雲都」。
units.en: Their armor was trimmed in black silk, and he named them the "Black Cloud Corps."
units.literal: Their armor and helmets were all adorned with black silk, and they were named the "Black Cloud Corps."

units.zh: 乾寧二年，行密盡有淮南之地，昭宗乃降制授行密淮南節度副大使知節度事、管內營田觀察處置等使、開府儀同三司、檢校太傅、同中書門下平章事、兼揚州大都督府長史、上柱國、宏農郡王，食邑三千戶，食實封一百戶。
units.en: In Qianning 2, Xingmi held all of Huainan. Emperor Zhaozong issued an edict making him vice military governor of Huainan with full authority, commissioner of farming, observation, and disposal, with the privilege of opening an office with honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, acting Grand Mentor, Grand Councillor, concurrent administrator of Yangzhou metropolis, Supreme Pillar of the State, and Prince of Hongnong, with a nominal fief of three thousand households and a substantive enfeoffment of one hundred.
units.literal: In the second year of Qianning, Xingmi held all the lands of Huainan; Zhaozong then issued an edict granting Xingmi appointment as vice military governor of Huainan with authority over the military governorship, commissioner for land reclamation, observation, and disposal within the circuit, with the privilege of opening an office and honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, acting Grand Mentor, jointly Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery, concurrent Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou metropolitan governor's office, Supreme Pillar of the State, and Prince of Hongnong Commandery, with a fief of three thousand households and a substantive fief of one hundred households.

units.zh: 四年，梁祖平兗、鄆，朱瑾及沙陀將李承嗣、史儼等皆奔淮南，行密待之優厚，任以為將，瑾與承嗣皆位至方伯。
units.en: In the fourth year the Liang Founder conquered Yan and Yun. Zhu Jin and the Shatuo officers Li Chengsi and Shi Yan fled to Huainan. Xingmi received them generously, made them generals, and Jin and Chengsi both rose to regional lord rank.
units.literal: In the fourth year the Liang Founder pacified Yan and Yun; Zhu Jin and the Shatuo generals Li Chengsi, Shi Yan, and others all fled to Huainan. Xingmi treated them generously and employed them as generals; Jin and Chengsi both rose to the rank of regional lord.

units.zh: 是歲，行密縱兵侵掠鄰部，兩浙錢镠、江西鐘傳、鄂州杜洪皆遣使求救於梁。
units.en: That year Xingmi's armies raided his neighbors. Qian Liu of the two Zhes, Zhong Chuan of Jiangxi, and Du Hong of Ezhou all sent envoys to the Liang for help.
units.literal: That year Xingmi let his troops raid neighboring circuits; Qian Liu of the two Zhes, Zhong Chuan of Jiangxi, and Du Hong of Ezhou all sent envoys begging rescue from the Liang.

units.zh: 梁祖遣朱友恭率部騎萬人渡江，取便討伐。
units.en: The Liang Founder sent Zhu Yougong with ten thousand horsemen across the Yangzi to strike wherever he could.
units.literal: The Liang Founder sent Zhu Yougong leading ten thousand cavalry of his command across the river to attack wherever opportunity offered.

units.zh: 行密先令都將翟章據黃州，及梁師至，即棄郡南渡，固守武昌寨，行密遣將馬珣以精兵五千助之，友恭與杜洪大破其眾，遂拔武昌寨，擒翟章並淮軍三千餘人，獲馬五百匹，淮夷大恐。
units.en: Xingmi had posted commander Zhai Zhang at Huangzhou, but when the Liang army came Zhang abandoned the city, crossed south, and held Wuchang Stockade. Xingmi sent Ma Xun with five thousand picked men to reinforce him. Yougong and Du Hong routed them, took the stockade, captured Zhai Zhang and more than three thousand Huai soldiers, seized five hundred horses, and panic spread through Huainan.
units.literal: Xingmi had first ordered the commander-in-chief Zhai Zhang to hold Huangzhou; when the Liang army arrived, Zhang immediately abandoned the prefecture, crossed south, and stubbornly defended Wuchang Stockade. Xingmi sent the general Ma Xun with five thousand elite troops to assist him. Yougong and Du Hong utterly defeated their host, then stormed Wuchang Stockade, captured Zhai Zhang together with more than three thousand Huai troops, took five hundred horses, and the Huai people were greatly terrified.

units.zh: 八月，梁祖遣葛從周領步騎萬人自霍丘渡淮，遣龐師古率大軍營於清口。
units.en: In the eighth month the Liang Founder sent Ge Congzhou with ten thousand foot and horse from Huoqiu across the Huai, and posted Pang Shigu with the main army at Qingkou.
units.literal: In the eighth month the Liang Founder sent Ge Congzhou leading ten thousand infantry and cavalry across the Huai from Huoqiu, and dispatched Pang Shigu with a great army to encamp at Qingkou.

units.zh: 淮人決堰縱水，流潦大至。
units.en: The Huai forces broke the dikes and let the floods rush in.
units.literal: The Huai men breached the dikes and released the water; flooding surged in greatly.

units.zh: 又令朱瑾率勁兵以襲汴軍，汴軍大敗，師古死之。
units.en: Zhu Jin then led elite troops against the Bian army. The Bian forces were routed and Shigu was killed.
units.literal: He also ordered Zhu Jin to lead crack troops to strike the Bian army; the Bian army was utterly defeated and Shigu died in the battle.

units.zh: 葛從周聞師古之敗，自濠梁班師，至淠河，為淮人所乘，諸軍僅得北歸。
units.en: Hearing of Shigu's defeat, Ge Congzhou withdrew from Haoliang, but at the Pi River the Huai caught him and his men barely escaped north.
units.literal: When Ge Congzhou heard of Shigu's defeat, he withdrew his army from Haoliang; reaching the Pi River he was set upon by the Huai men, and the armies barely made it back north.

units.zh: 光化二年，行密北侵，遣張歸厚禦之而退。
units.en: In Guanghua 2, Xingmi raided northward. The Liang sent Zhang Guihou against him and drove him back.
units.literal: In the second year of Guanghua, Xingmi invaded northward; the Liang sent Zhang Guihou to resist him and he withdrew.

units.zh: 天復三年，青州王師範叛，乞師於淮南，行密遣將王景仁率師二萬以援之，攻討密州。
units.en: In Tianfu 3, Wang Shifan of Qingzhou rebelled and asked Huainan for troops. Xingmi sent Wang Jingren with twenty thousand men to support him and besiege Mizhou.
units.literal: In the third year of Tianfu, Wang Shifan of Qingzhou rebelled and begged troops from Huainan; Xingmi sent the general Wang Jingren leading twenty thousand troops to aid him and attack Mizhou.

units.zh: 七月，梁祖大破師範及景仁之眾，景仁遁還，追至輔唐，殺數千人，進取密州。
units.en: In the seventh month the Liang Founder crushed Shifan and Jingren. Jingren fled, was chased to Futang, and thousands were killed before the Liang took Mizhou.
units.literal: In the seventh month the Liang Founder utterly defeated the hosts of Shifan and Jingren; Jingren fled back, was pursued to Futang, several thousand were killed, and the Liang advanced to take Mizhou.

units.zh: 天祐元年十一月，淮人攻光州，梁祖率軍抵霍丘，略地於廬、壽之境，淮人遁去。
units.en: In the eleventh month of Tianyou 1, Huainan attacked Guangzhou. The Liang Founder marched to Huoqiu and raided Luzhou and Shouzhou until the Huai forces withdrew.
units.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Tianyou, the Huai men attacked Guangzhou; the Liang Founder led his army to Huoqiu, raided territory in the Luzhou and Shouzhou region, and the Huai men fled away.

units.zh: 二年正月，進攻壽州，淮人閉壁不出，大掠而還。
units.en: In the first month of Tianyou 2 he attacked Shouzhou. The Huai shut themselves in, so he ravaged the countryside and withdrew.
units.literal: In the first month of the second year he advanced to attack Shouzhou; the Huai men shut their walls and would not come out, so he plundered greatly and returned.

units.zh: 是月，行密攻陷鄂州，擒節度使杜洪，戮於揚州市，梁之戍兵數千人亦陷焉。
units.en: That month Xingmi took Ezhou, captured military governor Du Hong, and executed him at Yangzhou. Several thousand Liang garrison troops fell with the city.
units.literal: That same month Xingmi stormed and captured Ezhou, seized the military governor Du Hong, and executed him in Yangzhou city; several thousand Liang garrison troops also perished there.

units.zh: 其後，江西鐘傳、宣州田頵俱為行密所並。
units.en: Afterward Xingmi absorbed both Zhong Chuan of Jiangxi and Tian Jun of Xuanzhou.
units.literal: Afterward, Zhong Chuan of Jiangxi and Tian Jun of Xuanzhou were both absorbed by Xingmi.

units.zh: 三年，行密以疾卒於廣陵。
units.en: In the third year Xingmi died of illness at Guangling.
units.literal: In the third year Xingmi died of illness at Guangling.

units.zh: 及其子渭僭號，偽追尊為太祖武皇帝。
units.en: When his son Wei declared himself emperor, the court of Wu posthumously honored him as Grand Ancestor Martial Emperor.
units.literal: When his son Wei usurped the imperial title, he was posthumously honored in the false state as Grand Ancestor Martial Emperor.

units.zh: 渥，字奉天，行密長子也。
units.en: Wo, courtesy name Fengtian, was Yang Xingmi's eldest son.
units.literal: Wo, style name Fengtian, was Xingmi's eldest son.

units.zh: 行密卒，渥遂襲偽位，自稱吳王，委軍政於大將張顥。
units.en: After Xingmi's death Wo took the Wu throne, styled himself King of Wu, and handed civil and military power to general Zhang Hao.
units.literal: When Xingmi died, Wo thereupon succeeded to the false throne, styled himself King of Wu, and entrusted military and civil affairs to the great general Zhang Hao.

units.zh: 渥性猜忌，不能禦下。
units.en: Wo was suspicious by nature and could not command his officers.
units.literal: Wo was suspicious by nature and could not control his subordinates.

units.zh: 天祐五年六月，渥為顥所殺，顥將納款於梁，遂自稱留後，委別將徐溫握兵柄。
units.en: In the sixth month of Tianyou 5, Zhang Hao killed Wo, planned to submit to the Liang, declared himself regent, and put deputy general Xu Wen in charge of the army.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Tianyou, Wo was killed by Hao; Hao was about to submit to the Liang, thereupon styled himself regent, and entrusted military power to the deputy general Xu Wen.

units.zh: 居無何，溫復殺顥，立行密次子渭為主。
units.en: Before long Xu Wen killed Hao as well and installed Xingmi's second son Wei as ruler.
units.literal: Before long, Wen again killed Hao and set up Xingmi's second son Wei as ruler.

units.zh: 及渭僭號，偽追尊為景帝。
units.en: When Wei declared himself emperor, Wo was posthumously honored as Emperor Jing.
units.literal: When Wei usurped the imperial title, he was posthumously honored in the false state as Emperor Jing.

units.zh: 渭，渥之弟也。
units.en: Wei was Wo's younger brother.
units.literal: Wei was Wo's younger brother.

units.zh: 既立，政事鹹委於徐溫。
units.en: Once enthroned, he left all government to Xu Wen.
units.literal: Once established on the throne, all government affairs were entrusted to Xu Wen.

units.zh: 時溫為鎮海軍節度、內外馬步軍都指揮使，乃於上元縣置升州，盛開幕府，自握兵柄於上流，其子知訓等於揚州居以秉政，凡十餘年。
units.en: Wen was military governor of Zhenhai and commander of all horse and foot. He set up Shengzhou in Shangyuan, built up a large staff, kept the army under his own hand upstream, and left his sons Zhixun and the rest at Yangzhou to run the government—for more than ten years.
units.literal: At that time Wen was military governor of Zhenhai army and overall commander of internal and external horse and foot forces; he then established Shengzhou in Shangyuan county, greatly opened a staff headquarters, himself held military power upstream, and his sons Zhixun and others resided at Yangzhou to wield government—for more than ten years in all.

units.zh: 溫乃冊渭為天子，國號大吳，改唐天祐十六年為武義元年。
units.en: Wen then enthroned Wei as emperor, named the state Great Wu, and declared the first year of Wuyi in place of Tang Tianyou 16.
units.literal: Wen then enthroned Wei as Son of Heaven, the state name was Great Wu, and the sixteenth year of Tang Tianyou was changed to the first year of Wuyi.

units.zh: 渭以溫為大丞相、都督中外諸軍事。
units.en: Wei made Xu Wen Grand Chancellor and supreme commander of all armies.
units.literal: Wei made Wen Grand Chancellor and commander-in-chief of all armies at home and abroad.

units.zh: 渭僭號凡三年而卒，謚為惠帝。
units.en: Wei reigned only three years before he died and was given the posthumous title Emperor Hui.
units.literal: Wei usurped the imperial title for only three years and then died; his posthumous title was Emperor Hui.

units.zh: 溥，行密幼子也。
units.en: Pu was Yang Xingmi's youngest son.
units.literal: Pu was Xingmi's youngest son.

units.zh: 初封丹陽王，渭卒，徐溫乃推溥為主，後僭偽號。
units.en: He was first made Prince of Danyang. When Wei died, Xu Wen put him on the throne, and he later declared himself emperor.
units.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Danyang; when Wei died, Xu Wen then pushed Pu forward as ruler, and afterward he usurped the false imperial title.

units.zh: 唐同光元年，莊宗平梁，遷都於洛陽。
units.en: In Tongguang 1, Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang conquered the Liang and moved the capital to Luoyang.
units.literal: In the first year of Tang Tongguang, Emperor Zhuangzong pacified the Liang and moved the capital to Luoyang.

units.zh: 十二月，溥遣使章景來朝，稱「大吳國主致書上大唐皇帝」，其辭旨卑遜，有同箋表。
units.en: In the twelfth month Pu sent Zhang Jing to court with a letter addressed to "the Great Tang Emperor" from "the Lord of Great Wu." The tone was abject, like a formal petition.
units.literal: In the twelfth month Pu sent the envoy Zhang Jing to court, addressing himself as "the Lord of Great Wu writes to present a letter to the Great Tang Emperor"; the tone was humble and submissive, much like a memorial missive.

units.zh: 明年八月，又遣其司農卿盧蘋貢方物，及獻貞簡太后珍玩，莊宗命左藏庫使王居敏、通事舍人張朗等以名馬報之。
units.en: The next year, in the eighth month, he sent Minister of Agriculture Lu Ping with local tribute and curios for Empress Dowager Zhenjian. Zhuangzong sent treasury officer Wang Jumin and relay officer Zhang Lang back with famous horses in return.
units.literal: In the eighth month of the following year he again sent his Minister of Agriculture Lu Ping to present local products and to offer rare treasures to Empress Dowager Zhenjian; Zhuangzong ordered the Left Treasury commissioner Wang Jumin, the memorial relay officer Zhang Lang, and others to respond with famous horses.

units.zh: 郭崇韜之平西川也，淮人大懼，將去偽號，稱藩於唐。
units.en: When Guo Chongtao conquered western Shu, Huainan was terrified and prepared to drop its imperial pretensions and submit as a Tang vassal.
units.literal: When Guo Chongtao pacified western Shu, the Huai people were greatly afraid and were about to abandon the false title and declare themselves a Tang vassal state.

units.zh: 時崇韜欲陳舟師下峽，為平吳之策，會崇韜既誅，洛城有變，淮人聞之，比屋相慶。
units.en: Chongtao had planned to send a fleet down the Yangzi gorges to conquer Wu, but he was executed and turmoil broke out in Luoyang. When Huainan heard the news, every household celebrated.
units.literal: At that time Chongtao wished to deploy a fleet down the gorges as a plan to pacify Wu; but just then Chongtao was already executed and turmoil arose in Luoyang—when the Huai people heard of it, household after household rejoiced together.

units.zh: 明宗纂嗣，溥復遣使修好，安重誨奏曰：「楊溥既不稱藩，無足與之抗禮，來偵國情，不如辭絕。」
units.en: When Mingzong took the throne, Pu sent envoys again. An Chonghui memorialized: "Yang Pu will not call himself a vassal, so he does not deserve equal ceremony. He comes to spy on us—we should refuse him."
units.literal: When Emperor Mingzong succeeded to the throne, Pu again sent envoys to renew friendly relations. An Chonghui memorialized, saying, "Since Yang Pu does not style himself a vassal, he is not worth receiving on equal ceremonial footing; he comes to spy on the state's affairs—it is better to refuse him."

units.zh: 乃謝其使，不受所貢，遣之。
units.en: The court turned the envoys away, refused their gifts, and sent them home.
units.literal: The court then declined his envoys, did not accept the tribute offered, and sent them away.

units.zh: 唐天成二年十月，徐溫卒，追封為齊王。
units.en: In the tenth month of Tiancheng 2, Xu Wen died and was posthumously made Prince of Qi.
units.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Tang Tiancheng, Xu Wen died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.

units.zh: 溫之養子李昪代溫佐輔，秉政數年，位至太尉、中書令、錄尚書事，襲封齊王，偽加九錫。
units.en: Wen's adopted son Li Bian took his place as chief minister, ruled for years, rose to Grand Marshal, Secretariat Director, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, inherited the title Prince of Qi, and received the Nine Bestowals in the Wu court.
units.literal: Wen's adopted son Li Bian replaced Wen in assisting governance, held power for several years, rose to Grand Marshal, Director of the Secretariat, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, succeeded to the enfeoffment as Prince of Qi, and in the false state was granted the Nine Bestowals.

units.zh: 晉天福二年，溥不得已遜位於昪。
units.en: In Tianfu 2 of Later Jin, Pu was forced to abdicate in Bian's favor.
units.literal: In the second year of Jin Tianfu, Pu under compulsion abdicated in favor of Bian.

units.zh: 昪遷溥於潤州，築丹陽宮以處之。
units.en: Bian moved Pu to Runzhou and built the Danyang Palace for him.
units.literal: Bian moved Pu to Runzhou and built the Danyang Palace to house him.

units.zh: 溥自是服羽衣，習辟谷之術，年餘以幽死。
units.en: Pu then took to Daoist robes and breatharian practice; a little over a year later he died in confinement.
units.literal: From then on Pu wore Daoist robes and practiced grain-avoidance techniques; after more than a year he died in seclusion.

units.zh: 昪又遷其族於海陵，吳人謂其居為永寧宮。
units.en: Bian then moved Pu's clan to Hailing, where the Wu people called their residence the Palace of Eternal Tranquility.
units.literal: Bian again moved his clan to Hailing; the people of Wu called their residence the Palace of Eternal Tranquility.

units.zh: 周顯德中，李景聞周師渡淮，慮氏為變，使人盡殺之。
units.en: During Zhou Xiande, Li Jing heard that Zhou armies had crossed the Huai. Fearing Pu's clan might rebel, he had them all killed.
units.literal: In the Xiande era of Zhou, Li Jing heard that Zhou troops had crossed the Huai, feared the clan might stir up trouble, and sent men to kill them all.

units.zh: 自唐大順二年，行密始有淮南之地，至溥遜位，凡四十七年而亡。
units.en: From Dashun 2, when Xingmi first held Huainan, until Pu's abdication, the Yang regime lasted forty-seven years.
units.literal: From the second year of Tang Dashun, when Xingmi first gained the Huainan region, until Pu's abdication, altogether forty-seven years passed and the state perished.

units.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：楊行密嘗命宣州刺史田頵領兵圍錢塘。
units.en: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》 records that Yang Xingmi once ordered Xuanzhou prefect Tian Jun to besiege Qiantang.
units.literal: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》 says: Yang Xingmi once ordered the Xuanzhou prefect Tian Jun to lead troops to besiege Qiantang.

units.zh: 錢珝危急，遣其子元皞修好於行密。
units.en: Qian Liu was in desperate straits and sent his son Yuanhao to sue for peace with Xingmi.
units.literal: Qian Liu was in dire peril and sent his son Yuanhao to seek good relations with Xingmi.

units.zh: 元頵風神俊邁，行密見之甚喜，因以其女妻之，遽命頵罷兵。
units.en: Yuanhao was striking and poised. Xingmi was delighted, gave him his daughter in marriage, and at once ordered Jun to lift the siege.
units.literal: Yuanhao was handsome in bearing and spirited; Xingmi was greatly pleased when he saw him and therefore gave him his daughter in marriage, and immediately ordered Jun to cease hostilities.

units.zh: 初，頵之圍城也，嘗遣使候錢珝起居，珝厚待之。
units.en: Earlier, during the siege, Jun had sent an envoy to inquire after Qian Liu's health, and Liu received him generously.
units.literal: Earlier, when Jun was besieging the city, he had once sent an envoy to inquire after Qian Liu's health; Liu treated him generously.

units.zh: 將行，復與之小飲，時羅隱、皮日休在坐，意以頵之師無能為也，且欲譏之。
units.en: Before the envoy left, Liu shared another cup with him. Luo Yin and Pi Rixiu were present, convinced Jun's army could do nothing and eager to mock him.
units.literal: As he was about to depart, Liu again drank a little with him; at the time Luo Yin and Pi Rixiu were seated there, thinking Jun's army could accomplish nothing and wishing moreover to mock him.

units.zh: 於是日休為令，取一字，四面被圍而不失其本音，因曰：「『其』字上加『鳷』為萁菜，下加『石』為鋋子，左加『玉』為琪玉，右加『月』為期會。」
units.en: Rixiu then proposed the rule: pick one character and add radicals on all four sides without changing how it is read. He said, "Put zhi above qi for 'bean stalk,' shi below for 'spearhead,' yu to the left for 'fine jade,' and yue to the right for 'appointed time.'"
units.literal: Thereupon Rixiu set the rule: take one character, surround it on four sides without losing its original pronunciation, and said, "Above the character qi add zhi to make ji vegetable; below add shi to make a spearhead; left add yu to make fine jade; right add yue to make a scheduled meeting."

units.zh: 羅隱取「於」字上加「雨」為舞雩，下加「皿」為盤盂，左加「玉」為於玉，右加「邑」為於阝地。
units.en: Luo Yin chose yu: rain above for 'rain sacrifice,' a vessel below for 'bowls and dishes,' jade to the left for 'jade ornament,' and a town radical to the right for 'place name.'
units.literal: Luo Yin took the character yu: above add rain for rain-dance sacrifice, below add vessel for platter and bowl, left add jade for yu-jade, right add settlement for yu-land.

units.zh: 使者取「亡」字譏錢镠必亡。
units.en: The envoy chose "wang" to imply that Qian Liu was doomed.
units.literal: The envoy took the character "wang" to mock that Qian Liu was sure to perish.

units.zh: 然「亡」上加「勣」為芒，下加「心」為忘，右加「邑」為邙，左加「心」為忙，其令不通，合坐皆嘻笑之，使大慚而去。
units.en: But wang with ji above gave mang, heart below gave 'forget,' a town radical right gave Mang mountain, heart left gave 'busy'—none of it worked. The whole table laughed, and the envoy left in shame.
units.literal: Yet above wang add ji to make mang, below add heart to make forget, right add settlement to make Mang hill, left add heart to make busy—the rule did not hold; all present laughed, and the envoy left in great shame.

units.zh: 未幾，頵果班師。
units.en: Before long Jun did withdraw his army.
units.literal: Before long, Jun indeed withdrew his army.

units.zh: 先是，行密與镠勢力相敵，其為忿怒，雖水火之不若也。
units.en: Before this, Xingmi and Qian Liu had been evenly matched rivals, and their mutual hatred burned hotter than fire against water.
units.literal: Earlier, Xingmi and Liu were matched in power; their mutual rage was fiercer even than fire and water.

units.zh: 行密嘗命以大索為錢貫，號曰「穿錢眼」，镠聞之，每歲命以大斧科柳，謂之「斫楊頭」。
units.en: Xingmi once had heavy ropes made into strings for Qian's coins and called them "piercing the coin's eye." Liu responded by having willows hacked each year with great axes and calling it "chopping Yang's head."
units.literal: Xingmi once ordered that great ropes be used as strings for Qian cash and called them "piercing the coin's eye"; when Liu heard of it, every year he ordered great axes to trim willows and called it "chopping Yang's head."

units.zh: 至是，以元蒨通婚，二境漸睦，穿眼、斫頭之論始止。
units.en: Now, through Yuanhao's marriage, the two realms grew friendly, and the taunts about piercing eyes and chopping heads finally stopped.
units.literal: At this time, because Yuanqian married into the family, the two territories gradually grew friendly, and talk of piercing eyes and chopping heads finally ceased.

units.zh: 李昪，本海州人。
units.en: Li Bian was a native of Haizhou.
units.literal: Li Bian was originally a man of Haizhou.

units.zh: 偽吳大丞相徐溫之養子也。
units.en: He was the adopted son of Xu Wen, Grand Chancellor of Wu.
units.literal: He was the adopted son of Xu Wen, Grand Chancellor of false Wu.

units.zh: 溫字敦美，亦海州人，初從淮南節度使楊行密起師於廬州，漸至軍校。
units.en: Xu Wen, courtesy name Dunmei, was also from Haizhou. He first followed Yang Xingmi when Xingmi raised his army at Luzhou and slowly rose to field officer.
units.literal: Wen, style name Dunmei, was also a man of Haizhou; he first followed the Huainan military governor Yang Xingmi in raising troops at Luzhou and gradually rose to army officer.

units.zh: 唐末，青州王師範為梁祖所圍，乞師於淮南，楊行密發兵赴之，溫時為小將，亦預其行。
units.en: In the late Tang, Wang Shifan of Qingzhou was besieged by the Later Liang founder. He asked Huainan for relief, and Yang Xingmi marched to his aid. Xu Wen was then a junior officer and went on the expedition as well.
units.literal: At the end of Tang, Qingzhou Wang Shifan was besieged by the Founding Ancestor of Liang; he begged troops from Huainan, and Yang Xingmi sent an army to go to his aid. Wen was at the time a junior officer and also took part in the expedition.

units.zh: 師次青之南鄙，師範已敗，淮兵大掠而還。
units.en: The army reached the southern edge of Qingzhou only to find Shifan already defeated. The Huainan troops plundered heavily and marched home.
units.literal: When the army halted at the southern marches of Qing, Shifan had already been defeated, and the Huai troops looted greatly and returned.

units.zh: 昪時幼稚，為溫所擄，溫愛其慧黠，遂育為己子，名曰知誥。
units.en: Li Bian was still a small boy when Xu Wen captured him. Wen was taken with the child's wit and intelligence and adopted him as his own son, giving him the name Zhigao.
units.literal: Bian was at the time still a child and was captured by Wen. Wen loved his cleverness and quick wit and therefore raised him as his own son, naming him Zhigao.

units.zh: 天祐初，行密卒，其子渥嗣，會左衛都指揮使張顥殺渥，欲歸命於梁。
units.en: Early in Tianyou, Yang Xingmi died and his son Wo succeeded him. Left Guard commander Zhang Hao then killed Wo and tried to surrender to the Liang.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianyou, Xingmi died and his son Wo succeeded. Then the Left Guard commander-in-chief Zhang Hao killed Wo and wished to submit to Liang.

units.zh: 溫謂顥曰：「此去梁國，往復三千里，不月餘事不成，軍國未有主，無主將亂，不如有所立，徐圖其事。」
units.en: Xu Wen told Zhang Hao, "The Liang capital is three thousand li away and back—we won't finish this in a month. The army and state have no master, and without one they will fall into chaos. Better to set someone up for now and pursue the rest at leisure."
units.literal: Wen said to Hao: "From here to the Liang state is three thousand li round trip; within little more than a month the affair will not be finished. The army and state have no ruler; without a ruler there will be chaos. It would be better to establish someone for the time being and gradually pursue the matter."

units.zh: 顥然之，乃立渥弟渭為帥。
units.en: Zhang Hao agreed, and they installed Wo's younger brother Wei as leader.
units.literal: Hao agreed, and they thereupon established Wo's younger brother Wei as commander.

units.zh: 溫尋殺顥，渭授溫常州刺史、檢校司徒。
units.en: Xu Wen soon killed Zhang Hao. Wei then made Wen prefect of Changzhou and acting Minister of Education.
units.literal: Wen soon killed Hao, and Wei appointed Wen prefect of Changzhou and acting Minister of Education.

units.zh: 溫留廣陵，遣昪知州事。
units.en: Xu Wen stayed at Guangling and put Li Bian in charge of the prefecture.
units.literal: Wen remained at Guangling and sent Bian to administer the prefecture.

units.zh: 是歲，唐天祐五年也。
units.en: That year was Tianyou 5 of the Tang.
units.literal: That year was the fifth year of Tang Tianyou.

units.zh: 七年，丁母憂，起復授檢校太尉、溫州刺史，充本州團練觀察使。
units.en: In the seventh year he went into mourning for his mother, was recalled to duty, and was made acting Grand Commandant and prefect of Wenzhou, with command of the prefecture's regimental training and observation forces.
units.literal: In the seventh year he entered mourning for his mother, was recalled from mourning, and was appointed acting Grand Commandant and prefect of Wenzhou, serving as regimental training and observation commissioner of that prefecture.

units.zh: 八年，宣州叛，溫與都將柴再用討平之，加同中書平章事，充淮南行軍司馬、內外馬步都指揮使、鎮海軍節度、浙江西道觀察等使。
units.en: In the eighth year Xuanzhou rebelled. Xu Wen and chief general Chai Zaiyong put down the revolt. He was made Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs, Huainan campaign deputy, commander of all cavalry and infantry, military governor of Zhenhai, and observation commissioner of Zhejiang West Circuit.
units.literal: In the eighth year Xuanzhou rebelled; Wen, together with the chief general Chai Zaiyong, suppressed and pacified it. He was promoted to Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs, and appointed Huainan campaign deputy, commander-in-chief of all internal and external cavalry and infantry, military governor of Zhenhai, and observation commissioner of Zhejiang West Circuit, among other posts.

units.zh: 十二年八月，溫出鎮潤州，以其子知訓知政事，加溫鎮海軍管內水陵馬步軍都軍使，兼寧國軍節度、宣歙池等州觀察使。
units.en: In the eighth month of the twelfth year Xu Wen took up his post at Runzhou and put his son Zhixun in charge of affairs of state. Wen was also made overall commander of Zhenhai's naval and land forces and concurrently military governor of Ningguo and observation commissioner of Xuan, She, Chi, and neighboring prefectures.
units.literal: In the eighth month of the twelfth year Wen went out to govern Runzhou and put his son Zhixun in charge of government affairs. Wen was further made overall commander of the naval, land, cavalry, and infantry forces within Zhenhai's jurisdiction, and concurrently military governor of Ningguo and observation commissioner of Xuan, She, Chi, and other prefectures.

units.zh: 時昪為溫屬郡升州刺史，乃大理郡廨，溫表移其府於金陵，偽授升州大都督府長史，充鎮海軍節度副大使，知節度事，以昪為鎮海軍節度副使、行潤州刺史，充本州團練使。
units.en: Li Bian was then prefect of Shengzhou, one of Wen's subordinate prefectures, and he rebuilt the prefectural offices on a grand scale. Wen petitioned to move his headquarters to Jinling and had himself appointed chief secretary of the Shengzhou Grand Protectorate, with the title of deputy military governor of Zhenhai and charge of military affairs. Bian was made deputy military governor of Zhenhai, acting prefect of Runzhou, and regimental training commissioner there.
units.literal: At the time Bian was prefect of Shengzhou, a prefecture under Wen's jurisdiction; he thereupon greatly repaired the prefectural offices. Wen memorialized to move his headquarters to Jinling and falsely appointed himself chief secretary of the Shengzhou Grand Protectorate, serving as deputy military governor of Zhenhai and administering military governorship affairs. Bian was made deputy military governor of Zhenhai, acting prefect of Runzhou, and regimental training commissioner of that prefecture.

units.zh: 十五年，知訓授淮南行軍副使、內外馬步軍都指揮使，通判軍府事。
units.en: In the fifteenth year Xu Zhixun was made Huainan campaign deputy and commander of all cavalry and infantry, with overall charge of military headquarters affairs.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year Zhixun was appointed Huainan campaign deputy, commander-in-chief of all internal and external cavalry and infantry, and given general charge of military headquarters affairs.

units.zh: 居無何，知訓為大將朱瑾所殺，溫以昪代知政事。
units.en: Before long, Xu Zhixun was killed by the general Zhu Jin, and Xu Wen put Li Bian in charge of government affairs in his place.
units.literal: Before long, Zhixun was killed by the great general Zhu Jin, and Wen had Bian replace him in managing government affairs.

units.zh: 明年，溫冊楊渭為天子，僭稱大吳，改唐天祐十六年為武義元年。
units.en: The next year Xu Wen enthroned Yang Wei as emperor. The Yang regime usurped the title Great Wu and changed Tianyou 16 to the first year of Wuyi.
units.literal: The next year Wen enthroned Yang Wei as Son of Heaven; he usurped the title Great Wu and changed Tang Tianyou sixteen to the first year of Wuyi.

units.zh: 十八年，渭死，溫聞之，自金陵馳歸揚州，夜入廣陵，議有所立。
units.en: In the eighteenth year Yang Wei died. When Xu Wen heard the news, he galloped from Jinling back to Yangzhou, entered Guangling by night, and debated whom to put on the throne.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year Wei died; when Wen heard of it he galloped from Jinling back to Yangzhou, entered Guangling by night, and deliberated on whom to enthrone.

units.zh: 或有希溫旨，言及蜀先主遺命諸葛亮之事，溫厲聲曰：「若楊氏無男，有女當立矣，無得異議。」
units.en: Some, hoping to curry favor with Xu Wen, brought up the Shu Former Lord's deathbed charge to Zhuge Liang. Wen snapped, "If the Yang house has no son, a daughter may be enthroned — and there will be no debate."
units.literal: Some who hoped to please Wen's intent spoke of the Former Lord of Shu's deathbed command to Zhuge Liang; Wen said sternly: "If the Yang house has no son, a daughter should be enthroned — no dissent will be tolerated."

units.zh: 由是群心乃定，遂迎丹陽王溥於潤州，以其年六月十八日即偽位，改元為順義。
units.en: With that the court settled. They brought Yang Pu, Prince of Danyang, to Runzhou, and on the eighteenth day of the sixth month he took the throne and adopted the era name Shunyi.
units.literal: Thereupon the minds of the multitude were settled; they thereupon welcomed the Prince of Danyang, Pu, at Runzhou, and on the eighteenth day of the sixth month of that year he assumed the false throne and changed the era name to Shunyi.

units.zh: 自是溫父子愈盛，中外共專其國，楊氏主祭而已。
units.en: From then on the Wen father and sons grew ever stronger and ran the realm inside and out, while the Yang clan performed rites and little else.
units.literal: From this time the Wen father and sons grew ever more powerful; within and without they jointly monopolized the state, and the Yang clan performed sacrifices only.

units.zh: 溫累官至竭忠定難建國功臣、大丞相、都督中外諸軍事、諸道都統、鎮海寧國等軍節度、宣歙池等州管內營田觀察等使、開府儀同三司、守太師、中書令、金陵尹、東海王，食邑一萬戶，實封五百戶。
units.en: Xu Wen rose to Merit Minister Who Exhausts Loyalty, Quells Disturbance, and Builds the State, Grand Chancellor, supreme commander of all armies, overall commander of all circuits, military governor of Zhenhai and Ningguo, farming and observation commissioner for Xuan, She, Chi, and neighboring prefectures, with the privilege of opening an office and honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, Acting Grand Preceptor, Secretariat Director, chief administrator of Jinling, and Prince of Donghai, with a nominal fief of ten thousand households and a substantive enfeoffment of five hundred.
units.literal: Wen rose in office to Merit Minister Who Exhausts Loyalty, Quells Disturbance, and Builds the State, Grand Chancellor, commander-in-chief of all armies at home and abroad, overall commander of all circuits, military governor of Zhenhai and Ningguo and other armies, commissioner of farming and observation within Xuan, She, Chi, and other prefectures, Bearer of the Golden Bellow and Grand Preceptor of the Palace, Acting Grand Preceptor, Director of the Secretariat, chief administrator of Jinling, Prince of Donghai, with a fief of ten thousand households and an actual enfeoffment of five hundred households.

units.zh: 偽順義七年改乾貞元年，即後唐天成二年。
units.en: In the seventh year of Shunyi the Wu court changed the era to Qianzhen 1, the same year as Later Tang Tiancheng 2.
units.literal: In the false state, the seventh year of Shunyi was changed to the first year of Qianzhen, which was the second year of Later Tang Tiancheng.

units.zh: 其年十月二十三日，溫卒，偽贈大元帥，追封齊王，謚曰忠武。
units.en: That year, on the twenty-third day of the tenth month, Xu Wen died. The Wu court posthumously made him Grand Marshal, enfeoffed him as Prince of Qi, and gave him the posthumous title Zhongwu.
units.literal: That year, on the twenty-third day of the tenth month, Wen died; in the false state he was posthumously invested as Grand Marshal, enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Qi, and given the posthumous title Zhongwu.

units.zh: 昪前夢溫負登山，逾年溫卒，昪乃偽授輔政興邦功臣，知內外左右事、開府儀同三同、守太尉、中書令、宣城公。
units.en: Li Bian had earlier dreamed that Xu Wen carried him up a mountain. A little over a year later Wen died, and Bian had himself invested as Merit Minister Who Assists the Government and Builds the State, with charge of all internal and external affairs, Grand Preceptor with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Departments, acting Grand Commandant, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke of Xuancheng.
units.literal: Li Bian had earlier dreamed that Xu Wen carried him up a mountain. A little over a year later Wen died, and Bian had himself invested as Merit Minister Who Assists the Government and Builds the State, with charge of all internal and external affairs, with the privilege of opening an office and honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, acting Grand Commandant, Secretariat Director, and Duke of Xuancheng.

units.zh: 昪自平朱瑾之亂，遂執吳政。
units.en: From the time Li Bian put down Zhu Jin's rebellion, he held the reins of the Wu regime.
units.literal: From the time Bian pacified Zhu Jin's rebellion, he thereupon held control of Wu government.

units.zh: 天成四年，偽吳改太和元年，是歲昪出鎮金陵，尋封東海王。
units.en: In Tiancheng 4 the Wu regime changed its era name to Taihe. That year Li Bian took up his post at Jinling and was soon enfeoffed as Prince of Donghai.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancheng, false Wu changed its era to Taihe 1. That year Bian went out to govern Jinling and was soon enfeoffed as Prince of Donghai.

units.zh: 至清泰二年改天祚元年，其年以金陵為齊國，封昪為齊王，乃追謚溫為忠武王，廟號太祖。
units.en: By Qingtai 2 the era had been changed to Tianzuo. That year Jinling was made the state of Qi, Li Bian was enfeoffed as Prince of Qi, and Xu Wen was posthumously honored as Taizu with the title King Zhongwu.
units.literal: By the second year of Qingtai the era was changed to Tianzuo 1. That year Jinling was made the state of Qi, Bian was enfeoffed as Prince of Qi, and Wen was posthumously given the temple name Taizu and the posthumous title King Zhongwu.

units.zh: 昪又進位太尉、錄尚書事，留鎮金陵，以其子景總政於揚州。
units.en: Li Bian was further promoted to Grand Commandant and Recorder of Affairs for the Department of State Affairs. He stayed at Jinling and put his son Jing in overall charge of government at Yangzhou.
units.literal: Bian was further promoted to Grand Commandant and Recorder of Affairs for the Department of State Affairs, remained to govern Jinling, and put his son Jing in overall charge of government at Yangzhou.

units.zh: 未幾，偽加昪九錫，建天子旌旗，改金陵為西都，以揚州為東都。
units.en: Before long he had Li Bian invested with the Nine Bestowals, granted him imperial banners and flags, made Jinling the Western Capital, and Yangzhou the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: Before long he falsely bestowed upon Bian the Nine Bestowals, erected the imperial banners and flags, changed Jinling to the Western Capital, and made Yangzhou the Eastern Capital.

units.zh: 昪開國依齊、梁故事。
units.en: Li Bian founded his state according to the precedents of Qi and Liang.
units.literal: Bian founded his state according to the precedents of Qi and Liang.

units.zh: 用徐玠為齊國右丞相，宋齊丘為左丞相，以為謀主。
units.en: He made Xu Jie Right Chancellor of Qi and Song Qiqiu Left Chancellor, and relied on them as his chief advisers.
units.literal: He employed Xu Jie as Right Chancellor of Qi and Song Qiqiu as Left Chancellor, taking them as his chief advisers.

units.zh: 偽吳天祚三年，楊溥遜位於昪，國號大齊，改元為升元，建都於金陵，時晉氏天福二年也。
units.en: In Tianzuo 3 of Wu, Yang Pu abdicated in favor of Li Bian. The state was renamed Great Qi, the era name was changed to Shengyuan, and the capital was set at Jinling—corresponding to Tianfu 2 under the Later Jin.
units.literal: In the third year of Tianzuo of false Wu, Yang Pu abdicated the throne to Bian. The state title was Great Qi, the era name was changed to Shengyuan, and the capital was established at Jinling; this was the second year of Tianfu of the Jin house.

units.zh: 昪乃冊楊溥為讓皇，其冊文曰「受禪老臣知誥，謹上冊皇帝為高尚思元宏古讓皇」云。
units.en: Li Bian then invested Yang Pu as the Abdication Emperor. The investiture text read, "The old minister who received the abdication, Zhigao, respectfully presents this investiture to the emperor as the Lofty, Virtuous, Reflective, Primordial, Grand, and Ancient Abdication Emperor."
units.literal: Bian thereupon enfeoffed Yang Pu as the Abdication Emperor; the investiture text read, "The old minister who received the abdication, Zhigao, respectfully presents this investiture to the emperor as the Lofty, Virtuous, Reflective, Primordial, Grand, and Ancient Abdication Emperor," and so forth.

units.zh: 仍以其子遙領平廬軍節度使，遷於海陵。
units.en: He also had Pu's son given the nominal post of military governor of Pinglu and moved him to Hailing.
units.literal: He still had Pu's son hold the title of military governor of Pinglu at a distance and moved him to Hailing.

units.zh: 昪自雲唐明皇第六子永王璘之裔。
units.en: Li Bian claimed descent from Prince Yong Li Lin, the sixth son of Emperor Xuanzong of Tang.
units.literal: Bian claimed for himself that he was a descendant of Prince Yong Li Lin, the sixth son of Tang Emperor Minghuang.

units.zh: 唐天寶末，安祿山連陷兩京，明皇幸蜀，詔以璘為山南、嶺南、黔中、江南四道節度采訪等使，璘至廣陵，大募兵甲，有窺圖江左之志，後為官軍所敗，死於大庾嶺北，故昪指之以為遠祖。
units.en: At the end of Tianbao, An Lushan seized both capitals and Emperor Xuanzong fled to Shu. An edict made Lin military governor and regional inspector of Shannan, Lingnan, Qianzhong, and Jiangnan. Lin reached Guangling, raised a large army, and set his sights on the lower Yangzi, but government forces defeated him and he died north of Dayu Ridge. Li Bian therefore claimed him as a distant ancestor.
units.literal: At the end of Tang Tianbao, An Lushan successively captured the two capitals; Emperor Minghuang took refuge in Shu and issued an edict appointing Lin military governor and regional inspector of the four circuits of Shannan, Lingnan, Qianzhong, and Jiangnan. Lin reached Guangling, greatly recruited armor and weapons, and had the ambition to seize the lands east of the Yangzi; later he was defeated by government troops and died north of Dayu Ridge. Therefore Bian pointed to him as a distant ancestor.

units.zh: 因還姓李氏，始改名昪，國號大唐，尊徐溫為義祖。
units.en: He then reclaimed the Li surname and took the name Bian. The state was renamed Great Tang, and Xu Wen was honored as Founding Ancestor by Right.
units.literal: Thereupon he restored the surname Li, first changing his name to Bian; the state title was Great Tang, and Xu Wen was honored as the Founding Ancestor by Right.

units.zh: 昪僭位凡七年，子景立。
units.en: Li Bian held the throne for seven years, and then his son Jing succeeded him.
units.literal: Bian usurped the throne for seven years altogether, and then his son Jing succeeded.

units.zh: 景，本名璟，及將臣於周，以犯廟諱，故改之。
units.en: Jing's original given name used the character meaning 'fine jade'; when he was about to pay court to Zhou he changed it because it violated the dynastic taboo.
units.literal: Jing, original given name Jing (the character for fine jade), when about to pay court to Zhou changed it because it violated the temple taboo.

units.zh: 昪之長子也，
units.en: He was Li Bian's eldest son,
units.literal: He was Bian's eldest son,

units.zh: 〈（《釣磯立談》云：烈祖一日晝寢，夢一黃龍出殿之西楹，矯首內向，如窺伺狀。
units.en: (The 《Diaoji Litán》 records that one day the Founding Ancestor napped at midday and dreamed of a yellow dragon emerging from the hall's western pillar, raising its head and turning inward as if watching something.
units.literal: (The 《Diaoji Litán》 says: One day the Founding Ancestor napped at midday and dreamed that a yellow dragon emerged from the western pillar of the hall, raised its head and turned inward, as if peering and watching.

units.zh: 烈祖驚起，使人偵之，顧見元宗方倚楹而立，遣人候上動靜，於是立嫡之意遂決。）〉
units.en: The Founding Ancestor woke with a start and sent men to investigate. He found Yuanzong leaning against a pillar, with attendants posted to watch his movements. From that moment his decision to name the legitimate heir was made.)〉
units.literal: The Founding Ancestor started up in alarm and sent men to investigate; looking back, he saw that Yuanzong was just then leaning against a pillar and standing, having sent men to watch the sovereign's movements. Thereupon the intention to establish the legitimate heir was decided.)〉

units.zh: 昪卒，乃襲偽位，改元為保大。
units.en: When Li Bian died, Jing succeeded to the throne and changed the era name to Baoda.
units.literal: When Bian died, Jing thereupon succeeded to the usurped throne and changed the era name to Baoda.

units.zh: 以仲弟遂為皇太弟，季弟達為齊王，仍於父柩前設盟約，兄弟相繼。
units.en: He made his second brother Sui Imperial Younger Brother and his youngest brother Da Prince of Qi. Before their father's coffin they swore a covenant that the brothers would succeed one another in turn.
units.literal: He made his second younger brother Sui Imperial Younger Brother, his youngest younger brother Da Prince of Qi, and still before their father's coffin established a covenant that the brothers would succeed one another in turn.

units.zh: 景僭號之後，屬中原多事，北土亂離，雄據一方，行余一紀。
units.en: After Jing took the imperial title, the Central Plains were in turmoil and the north was in chaos. He held his ground as a regional power for more than twelve years.
units.literal: After Jing usurped the imperial title, it happened that the Central Plains were beset by many affairs and the northern lands were torn by disorder; he held one region in dominance for more than twelve years.

units.zh: 其地東暨衢、婺，南及五嶺，西至湖湘，北據長淮，凡三十餘州，廣袤數千里，盡為其所有，近代僭竊之地，最為強盛。
units.en: His realm stretched east to Quzhou and Wuzhou, south to the Five Ridges, west to Hunan and the Xiang basin, and north to the Huai River—more than thirty prefectures across thousands of li, all under his control. Among the separatist states of recent times, none was stronger.
units.literal: His territory extended east to Qu and Wu, south to the Five Ridges, west to Hunan and the Xiang region, and north to the Long Huai; altogether more than thirty prefectures, several thousand li in breadth and length—all were his possession. Among the usurped domains of recent times, his was the strongest.

units.zh: 又嘗遣使私賂契丹，俾為中國之患，自固偷安之計。
units.en: He also sent secret envoys to bribe the Khitan, hoping they would harry the Central Plains and leave him secure in his own complacency.
units.literal: He also once sent envoys to bribe the Khitan in secret, so that they would become a calamity for China—his own plan to secure himself in ease and complacency.

units.zh: 〈（《南唐書》云：契丹遣二使來告曰：「晉少主逆命背約，自貽廢黜，吾主欲與唐繼先世之好，將冊君為中原主。」
units.en: (The 《History of Southern Tang》 records that the Khitan sent two envoys with this message: "The Later Jin emperor defied his obligations and brought deposition on himself. Our lord wishes to renew the old friendship with Tang and will invest you as ruler of the Central Plains."
units.literal: (The 《History of Southern Tang》 says: The Khitan sent two envoys to announce: "The Later Jin young lord defied orders and broke the covenant, bringing his own deposition upon himself. Our lord wishes to renew the friendship of former generations with Tang and will invest you as sovereign of the Central Plains."

units.zh: 嗣主曰：「孤守江、淮，社稷已固，與梁、宋阻隔。
units.en: The Successor Lord replied, "I hold the Yangzi and Huai, my realm is already secure, and I am separated from Liang and Song by distance.
units.literal: The Successor Lord said: "I hold the Yangzi and Huai; my altars of soil and grain are already secure, and I am cut off from Liang and Song by distance.

units.zh: 若爾主不忘先好，惠賜行人，受賜多矣，其他不敢拜命之辱。」）〉
units.en: If your lord remembers our old friendship and honors my envoys with gifts, that is gift enough. As for the rest, I dare not accept so humiliating a commission.")〉"
units.literal: If your lord does not forget the former friendship and graciously bestows gifts on my envoys, I have already received more than enough favor; as for the rest, I dare not accept the humiliation of bowing to such a commission.")〉"

units.zh: 周顯德二年冬，世宗始議南征，以宰臣李穀為前軍都部署。
units.en: In the winter of Xiande 2, Emperor Shizong of Zhou began planning a southern campaign and made chief minister Li Gu overall commander of the vanguard.
units.literal: In the winter of the second year of Zhou Xiande, Emperor Shizong first deliberated a southern campaign and appointed the chief minister Li Gu overall commander of the vanguard army.

units.zh: 是冬，周師圍壽春。
units.en: That winter Zhou armies besieged Shouchun.
units.literal: That winter, Zhou troops besieged Shouchun.

units.zh: 三年春，世宗親征淮甸，大敗淮寇於正陽，遂進攻壽州。
units.en: In the spring of the third year the emperor led the campaign in person in the Huai region, routed the Huai enemy at Zhengyang, and then pressed the attack on Shouzhou.
units.literal: In the spring of the third year the emperor personally campaigned in the Huai region, greatly defeated the Huai bandits at Zhengyang, and thereupon advanced to attack Shouzhou.

units.zh: 尋又今上敗何延錫於渦口，擒皇甫暉於滁州。
units.en: Soon after, Zhao Kuangyin routed He Yanshi at Wokou and captured Huangfu Hui at Chuzhou.
units.literal: Soon after, the present sovereign defeated He Yanshi at Wokou and captured Huangfu Hui at Chuzhou.

units.zh: 景聞之大懼，遣其臣鐘謨、李德明等奉表於世宗，乞為附庸之國，仍歲貢百萬之數，又進金銀器幣及犒軍牛酒。
units.en: Jing was terrified. He sent his ministers Zhong Mo and Li Deming with a memorial to Shizong, begging to become a vassal state and offering a million in annual tribute, along with gold and silver vessels and currency and cattle and wine to reward the army.
units.literal: When Jing heard of this he was greatly afraid and sent his ministers Zhong Mo, Li Deming, and others to present a memorial to Shizong, begging to become a vassal state and still to pay tribute of one million per year; he also presented gold, silver, vessels, and currency, together with cattle and wine to reward the army.

units.zh: 未幾，又遣其臣孫晟、王崇質等奉表修貢，且言：「景願割濠、壽、泗、楚、光、海等六州之地，隸於大朝，乞罷攻討。」
units.en: Soon he sent Sun Sheng, Wang Chongzhi, and others with another memorial, offering to cede Hao, Shou, Si, Chu, Guang, and Hai to the Zhou and begging them to stop the campaign."
units.literal: Before long he again sent his ministers Sun Sheng, Wang Chongzhi, and others to present a memorial renewing tribute, and moreover said, "Jing wishes to cede the territory of the six prefectures Hao, Shou, Si, Chu, Guang, and Hai to be subject to the Great Court, and begs that the attack be halted."

units.zh: 世宗未之許。
units.en: Shizong refused.
units.literal: Shizong did not grant it.

units.zh: 時李德明等見周師爭攻壽春，慮不能保，乃奏云：「寬臣等五日之誅，容臣等自往江南，取本國表章，舉江北諸州，盡獻於大朝。」
units.en: Li Deming and his colleagues, seeing Shouchun hard pressed, feared all was lost and pleaded: "Give us five days' grace; let us return to Jiangnan, bring back our ruler's formal submission, and surrender every prefecture north of the Yangzi."
units.literal: At that time Li Deming and the others, seeing Zhou troops pressing the attack on Shouchun and fearing it could not be held, memorialized, saying, "Grant us five days' reprieve from execution; allow us to go ourselves to Jiangnan, obtain our state's formal memorial, and offer all the prefectures north of the river to the Great Court."

units.zh: 世宗許其行。
units.en: Shizong let them go.
units.literal: Shizong permitted their journey.

units.zh: 久之，德明等不至，乃權議回鑾，惟留偏師數千圍守壽春而已。
units.en: When Deming failed to return, Shizong decided to withdraw, leaving only a few thousand men to keep Shouchun under siege.
units.literal: After a long while Deming and the others did not arrive; the court then provisionally resolved to withdraw the imperial carriage, leaving only a detached force of several thousand to besiege and hold Shouchun.

units.zh: 四年春，世宗再駕南征。
units.en: In the spring of the fourth year Shizong marched south again in person.
units.literal: In the spring of the fourth year Shizong again personally led a southern campaign.

units.zh: 三月，大敗江南援軍於紫金山，尋下壽州，乃命班師。
units.en: In the third month he routed the Jiangnan relief force at Purple Gold Mountain, took Shouchun, and ordered the army to withdraw.
units.literal: In the third month he utterly defeated the Jiangnan relief army at Purple Gold Mountain, soon afterward captured Shouchun, and then ordered the army to withdraw.

units.zh: 是歲冬十月，世宗復臨淮甸，連下濠、泗二郡，進攻楚州。
units.en: That winter, in the tenth month, Shizong returned to the Huai country, took Hao and Si in succession, and advanced on Chuzhou.
units.literal: In the tenth month of winter that year Shizong again came to the Huai region, captured the two prefectures Hao and Si in succession, and advanced to attack Chuzhou.

units.zh: 明年春正月，拔之，遂移幸揚州，駐大軍於迎鑾，將議濟江。
units.en: The next spring he took Chuzhou, moved to Yangzhou, massed his army at Yingluan, and prepared to cross the Yangzi.
units.literal: In the first month of spring the following year he stormed it, then moved the court to Yangzhou, stationed the great army at Yingluan, and was about to discuss crossing the river.

units.zh: 景聞之，自謂亡在朝夕，乃謀欲傳位其世子，使稱藩於周。
units.en: Jing believed his end was near and planned to abdicate in favor of his heir and submit to Zhou as a vassal.
units.literal: When Jing heard of this he thought himself doomed within days, and therefore plotted to pass the throne to his heir and have him declare vassalage to Zhou.

units.zh: 〈（《南唐書》：正月，改無交泰。）〉
units.en: (The 《History of Southern Tang》 records that in the first month the era name was changed to Jiaotai.)
units.literal: (The 《History of Southern Tang》: in the first month, the era was changed to Jiaotai.)

units.zh: 遣其臣陳覺奉表陳情，且順世宗之旨焉。
units.en: He sent Chen Jue with a memorial pleading his case and bowing to Shizong's will.
units.literal: He sent his minister Chen Jue to present a memorial stating his case and to comply with Shizong's intent.

units.zh: 覺至，世宗召對於禦幄。
units.en: When Jue arrived, Shizong received him in the imperial tent.
units.literal: When Jue arrived, Shizong summoned him for audience in the imperial tent.

units.zh: 是時江北諸州，唯廬、舒、蘄、黃四郡未下，世宗因謂覺曰：「江南國主若能以江北之地盡歸於我，則朕亦不至窮兵黷武。」
units.en: Only Lu, Shu, Qi, and Huang north of the Yangzi still held out. Shizong told Jue, "If your master surrenders all the north bank, I will not grind on with endless war."
units.literal: At that time of all the prefectures north of the river, only the four districts Lu, Shu, Qi, and Huang had not fallen; Shizong thereupon said to Jue, "If the lord of Jiangnan can return all the territory north of the river to Us, then We too will not exhaust the armies in excessive warfare."

units.zh: 覺聞命欣然，即遣人過江取景表，以廬、舒、蘄、黃等四州來上，乞畫江為界，仍歲貢地征數十萬。
units.en: Jue gladly crossed the river for Jing's formal submission, offering Lu, Shu, Qi, and Huang, asking that the Yangzi be the border and promising several hundred thousand in annual land tax.
units.literal: Jue heard the command with delight, immediately sent men across the river to obtain Jing's memorial, and offered the four prefectures Lu, Shu, Qi, and Huang; he begged to take the river as boundary and still to pay several hundred thousand in annual land tax.

units.zh: 世宗許之，乃還京。
units.en: Shizong agreed and returned to the capital.
units.literal: Shizong granted it and then returned to the capital.

units.zh: 自是景始行大朝正朔，上章稱唐國主臣景，累遣使修貢，亦不失外臣之禮焉。
units.en: From then on Jing adopted the Zhou calendar, styled himself "Minister Jing, Lord of Tang," sent tribute repeatedly, and observed every courtesy owed a vassal.
units.literal: From then on Jing began to follow the Great Court's calendar, submitted memorials styling himself "Minister Jing, Lord of the Tang state," repeatedly sent envoys to renew tribute, and did not fall short of the rites due a foreign minister.

units.zh: 皇朝建隆二年夏，景以疾卒於金陵，時年四十六。
units.en: In the summer of Jianlong 2 of the Song, Jing died of illness at Jinling at the age of forty-six.
units.literal: In the summer of the second year of Jianlong of Our Dynasty, Jing died of illness at Jinling, aged forty-six.

units.zh: 以其子煜襲偽位，其後事具皇家日曆。
units.en: His son Yu took the throne; later events are recorded in the imperial annals.
units.literal: His son Yu succeeded to the false throne; his later affairs are fully recorded in the imperial calendar.

units.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：李掞，本為徐溫所養，溫殺張顥，權出於己，自稱大丞相、中書令、都統。
units.en: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》 records that Li Bian, then called Li Shan, was Xu Wen's adopted son. After Wen killed Zhang Hao he seized power as Grand Chancellor, Secretariat Director, and supreme commander.
units.literal: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》 says: Li Shan was originally raised by Xu Wen; Wen killed Zhang Hao, power issued from himself, and he styled himself Grand Chancellor, Director of the Secretariat, and overall commander.

units.zh: 及出居金陵，以嫡子知訓為丞相，掞為潤州節度。
units.en: When he moved to Jinling he made his son Zhixun chancellor and Shan military governor of Runzhou.
units.literal: When he went out to reside at Jinling, he made his legitimate son Zhixun chancellor and Shan military governor of Runzhou.

units.zh: 掞始為宣州，忽得潤州，甚怏怏，將白溫辭之。
units.en: Shan had governed Xuanzhou and was displeased to be shifted to Runzhou; he was about to ask Wen to release him.
units.literal: Shan had first been at Xuanzhou; suddenly receiving Runzhou, he was very displeased and was about to inform Wen and resign the post.

units.zh: 宋齊丘素與掞善，因謂掞曰：「知訓驕倨，不可大用，殆必有損足焚巢之患。
units.en: Song Qiqiu, who was close to Shan, told him, "Zhixun is arrogant and unfit for high office; he will burn down his own nest.
units.literal: Song Qiqiu had long been on good terms with Shan and therefore said to him, "Zhixun is arrogant and haughty and cannot be greatly employed; he will likely bring the calamity of scorching the nest by warming the feet.

units.zh: 宣州去江都遠，難為應，潤州方隔一水爾，有急則可以立功，慎勿辭也。」
units.en: Xuanzhou is too far from the capital to help in a crisis, but Runzhou is just across the water—you can save the day if trouble comes. Do not resign."
units.literal: Xuanzhou is far from Jiangdu and hard to respond from; Runzhou is only separated by one stretch of water—if there is urgency you can win merit. Take care not to resign."

units.zh: 昪聞之釋然，遂行。
units.en: Bian took heart and went.
units.literal: When Bian heard this he was relieved and set out.

units.zh: 至潤州，未幾知訓果為朱瑾所殺，是夜，江都亂，火光亙天，掞望之曰：「宋公之言中矣。」
units.en: At Runzhou he soon learned Zhixun had been killed by Zhu Jin. That night Jiangdu blazed with fire. Shan looked across the water and said, "Song was right."
units.literal: When he reached Runzhou, before long Zhixun was indeed killed by Zhu Jin; that night Jiangdu was in turmoil and firelight filled the sky. Shan gazed at it and said, "Master Song's words have hit the mark."

units.zh: 遂引軍渡江，盡誅朱瑾之黨。
units.en: He crossed the river with his army and exterminated Zhu Jin's faction.
units.literal: He thereupon led his army across the river and executed to the last the faction of Zhu Jin.

units.zh: 後解甲去備，以待徐溫。
units.en: Then he laid aside armor and guard to await Xu Wen.
units.literal: Afterward he doffed armor and removed his guard, waiting for Xu Wen.

units.zh: 溫至，且喜且怒，謂掞曰：「猶幸汝在潤州，不然吾家大勢將去矣。
units.en: Wen arrived, both grateful and angry, and told Shan, "Thank heaven you were at Runzhou, or our house would have been finished.
units.literal: When Wen arrived, both pleased and angry, he said to Shan, "Fortunately you were at Runzhou—otherwise the great momentum of our house would have been lost.

units.zh: 汝於兄弟中有大功者耶！」
units.en: You have done the greatest service of all my sons!"
units.literal: Among the brothers you have rendered the greatest merit!"

units.zh: 即日用掞為左僕射，知政事，以代知訓。
units.en: That same day he made Shan Left Vice Director and head of government, in Zhixun's place.
units.literal: That very day he appointed Shan Left Vice Director and supervisor of government affairs, to replace Zhixun.

units.zh: 掞善於撫禦，內外之心翕然而歸之，故徐溫卒未幾而江南遂為掞所有。
units.en: Shan won men over inside and out, and not long after Xu Wen's death all Jiangnan fell into his hands.
units.literal: Shan was skilled at comforting and controlling men; hearts within and without converged upon him, and therefore not long after Xu Wen died Jiangnan came to belong to Shan.

units.zh: 先是，江南童謠云：「東海鯉魚飛上天。」
units.en: A Jiangnan children's rhyme had run, "The Eastern Sea carp flies up to heaven."
units.literal: Earlier, a children's rhyme in Jiangnan ran, "The carp of the Eastern Sea flies up to heaven."

units.zh: 東海即徐之望也，鯉者李也，蓋言李掞一旦自溫家起而為君爾。
units.en: "Eastern Sea" pointed to the Xu clan's homeland; "carp" (li) meant Li—foretelling that Li Bian would rise from the Xu house to become ruler.
units.literal: Eastern Sea is Xu's origin; carp means Li—it meant that Li Shan would one day rise from the Xu household to become ruler.

units.zh: 初，掞既蓄異志，且欲諷動僚屬。
units.en: Shan had long harbored larger ambitions and wanted to sound out his staff.
units.literal: At first Shan had already harbored a different intent and wished moreover to move his subordinates by insinuation.

units.zh: 雪天大會，酒酣，出一令，須借雪取古人名，仍詞理通貫。
units.en: At a snowy banquet, when the wine was flowing, he proposed a drinking game: use "snow" in a riddle naming a historical figure, with coherent wording.
units.literal: On a snowy day he held a great gathering; when the wine was warm he proposed a rule: one must take snow to form an ancient person's name, and the wording still had to be coherent.

units.zh: 時齊丘、徐融在坐，掞舉杯為令曰：「雪下紛紛，便是白起。」
units.en: Qiqiu and Xu Rong were present. Shan raised his cup and said, "Snow falling thick—that's Bai Qi (White Rise)."
units.literal: At the time Qiqiu and Xu Rong were seated; Shan raised his cup and set the rule, saying, "Snow falling in profusion—that is Bai Qi."

units.zh: 齊丘曰：「著屐過街，必須雍齒。」
units.en: Qiqiu answered, "Clogs in the street—that's Yong Chi (Yong Teeth)."
units.literal: Qiqiu said, "Wearing clogs to cross the street—that must be Yong Chi."

units.zh: 融意欲挫掞等，遽曰：「明朝日出，爭奈蕭何。」
units.en: Rong, trying to cut them down, shot back, "When the sun rises tomorrow—what about Xiao He?" implying their day would end."
units.literal: Rong wished to humble Shan and the others and blurted, "When the sun comes out tomorrow, what can be done about Xiao He?"

units.zh: 掞大怒，是夜收融投於江，自是與謀者惟齊丘而已。
units.en: Shan was furious. That night he had Rong thrown into the river, and afterward Qiqiu alone shared his plots.
units.literal: Shan was greatly enraged; that night he seized Rong and cast him into the river, and from then on his only fellow plotter was Qiqiu.

units.zh: 宋齊丘，豫章人，父嘗在鐘傳幕下。
units.en: Song Qiqiu was from Yuzhang. His father had once served under Zhong Chuan.
units.literal: Song Qiqiu was a man of Yuzhang; his father had once served on Zhong Chuan's staff.

units.zh: 齊丘素落魄，父卒，家計蕩盡，已在窮悴，朝夕不能度。
units.en: Qiqiu had always been down on his luck. After his father died the family fortune vanished and he was destitute, barely surviving day to day.
units.literal: Qiqiu had always been down on his luck; when his father died the family fortune was utterly spent, and he was already in destitution, unable to get through from morning to night.

units.zh: 時姚洞天為淮南騎將，素好士，齊丘欲謁之，且囊空無備紙筆之費，計無所出，但於逆旅社門而坐，如此殆數日。
units.en: Yao Dongtian, a Huainan cavalry officer who loved scholars, was someone Qiqiu wanted to meet, but he had no money even for paper and ink. For days he simply sat at the inn gate, unable to think of a way forward.
units.literal: At that time Yao Dongtian was a Huainan cavalry officer and by nature loved scholars; Qiqiu wished to call on him, yet his purse was empty and he had no money to prepare paper and brush; finding no way out, he only sat at the gate of the inn's lodge, thus for nearly several days.

units.zh: 鄰房有散樂女尚幼，問齊丘曰：「秀才何以數日不出？」
units.en: A young traveling entertainer in the next room asked him, "Scholar, why haven't you left your room for days?"
units.literal: In the neighboring room was a young female performer of itinerant music still a child; she asked Qiqiu, "Scholar, why have you not gone out for several days?"

units.zh: 齊丘以實告，女嘆曰：「此甚小事，秀才何吝一言相示耶！」
units.en: He told her the truth. She sighed and said, "That's nothing—you only had to ask!"
units.literal: Qiqiu told her the truth; the girl sighed and said, "This is a very small matter—Scholar, why be stingy about speaking a word to show it!"

units.zh: 乃惠以數緡。
units.en: She gave him a few strings of cash.
units.literal: She then gave him several strings of cash as a kindness.

units.zh: 齊丘用市紙筆，為詩詠以投洞天，其略曰：「某學武無成，攻文失誌，歲華蹭蹬，身事蹉跎。
units.en: Qiqiu bought paper and brush and sent Dongtian a poem that began, "I studied arms without success and letters without reward; the years slip by and my life goes nowhere.
units.literal: Qiqiu used them to buy paper and brush, composed a poem to present to Dongtian, the gist of which ran, "I studied arms without success, pursued letters and lost my aim; the years slip stumbling by, and my life's affairs drag in delay.

units.zh: 胸中之萬仞青山，壓低氣宇；
units.en: Ten-thousand-ren green mountains in my breast weigh down my spirit;
units.literal: The ten-thousand-ren green mountains in my breast press down my spirit;

units.zh: 頭上之一輪紅日，燒盡風雲。
units.en: one red sun above my head burns away every storm;
units.literal: the one round red sun upon my head burns away wind and clouds;

units.zh: 加以天步淩遲，皇綱廢絕，四海淵黑，中原血紅。
units.en: Heaven itself staggers, imperial order lies in ruins, the four seas sink into darkness, the heartland runs red with blood;
units.literal: moreover Heaven's step falters, the royal net is abolished, the four seas are abyss-deep black, the Central Plains blood-red;

units.zh: 挹飛蒼走黃之辯，有出鬼沒神之機。」
units.en: I wield a huntsman's eloquence and a wit that appears and vanishes like spirits."
units.literal: I draw on the disputation of 'flying azure' and 'running yellow,' and possess stratagems that emerge like ghosts and vanish like spirits."

units.zh: 洞天怒其言大，不即接見。
units.en: Dongtian took offense at such grand language and refused to see him at once.
units.literal: Dongtian was angered that his words were too grand and did not immediately receive him.

units.zh: 齊丘窘急，乃更其啟，翌日復至，其略曰：「有生不如無生，為人不若為鬼。」
units.en: Desperate, Qiqiu rewrote his letter and came back the next day with a plea that ran, "Better never to have lived than to live; better to be a ghost than a man."
units.literal: Qiqiu, in distress, rewrote his letter and returned the next day; the gist ran, "To live is not as good as not to live; to be human is not as good as being a ghost."

units.zh: 又云：「其為誠懇萬端，只為饑寒兩字。」
units.en: He added, "My earnestness knows no end--all for two words: hunger and cold."
